properties.areaDesc: Mineral, CO; Rio Grande, CO; Saguache, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 5:59PM MDT until October 22 at 10:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
Heavy rainfall is causing flooding along the South Fork of the Rio
Grande, which is forecast to crest at 9.2 feet around 1 AM tonight.
If you live near the South Fork of the Rio Grande, and the main stem
of the Rio Grande, take precautions to protect life and property from
flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Saguache, Central Mineral and Western Rio
Grande Counties...

* WHEN...Until 1015 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Several
structures are flooded and some sand bagging operations are
continuing. Streams continue to rise due to excess runoff from
continued rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 552 PM MDT, South Fork Fire and Colorado State Patrol report
continued rainfall across the warned area.
- Water is currently near Highway 160 at Wolf Creek Ranch at mile
marker 177.  Several homes are also being flooded in the South
Fork area.  The river gauge on the south fork of the Rio Grande
(SRGC2) is rapidly rising, and forecast to crest at 9.2 feet by 1
AM tonight, and slowly fall during the overnight hours.  The main
stem of the Rio Grande will likely run high down toward Del
Norte.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Del Norte, South Fork, Wagon Wheel Gap, Wolf Creek Pass and
Creede.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Interior Kuskokwim Delta; Western Capes; Northern Bristol Bay Coast
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 22 at 3:54PM AKDT until October 24 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 35 to 50 mph with gusts up to 75
mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, Platinum and Goodnews Bay, and Northern
Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Friday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are expected to start by 1
PM AKDT Friday for the Kuskokwim Delta, Northern Bristol Bay,
Platinum, and Goodnews Bay. For the Western Capes, the strongest
winds are expected near Cape Newenham, with winds for Platinum and
Goodnews Bay expected to be near 60 mph. For Northern Bristol Bay,
the strongest winds are expected near Togiak, while gusts up to 50
mph are expected for Dillingham. Winds are expected to steadily
diminish through Saturday as the front moves inland and weakens.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must drive.
